title: Week-2-DFS-Complete-Dossier
universal_lens: The dossier formalizes a high-dimensional constraint satisfaction problem over a discrete roster space. It unifies second-party salary priors, environmental perturbations (wind/rain), and injury-induced state transitions into a singular expected value operator, mapping raw athletic output to a probabilistic payout manifold. The structural unification of DFS valuation relies on the tensor product of scheme-specific exposure vectors and defensive grading manifolds. By mapping player usage probabilities onto a high-dimensional constraint space, we isolate orthogonal value axes where market pricing fails to account for non-linear game-script dependencies.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats the [2P] salary tags as noisy proxies for true market consensus. Bayesian updating is applied when Akamai blocks occur or official inactives drop at 11:30 AM CT, dynamically recalibrating conformal prediction intervals around projected fantasy points and ownership percentages. GSI employs conformal inference to bound the expected fantasy points (XFP) under distributional shifts. We treat scheme alignment as a covariate shift, calculating prediction intervals that dynamically adjust for defensive grading anomalies, ensuring robust probabilistic guarantees against overfitting to small-sample Week 1 data.
gse_mapping: GSE models the slate as a directed acyclic graph of situational states. Weather conditions act as edge weights suppressing deep passing probabilities, while injuries like Okonkwo's absence trigger immediate vacuum effects, mathematically redistributing target shares across remaining valid nodes. GSE models the game as a continuous-time Markov decision process. State transitions are driven by tempo metrics and play-action frequencies. The engine evaluates optimal stopping times for roster construction by maximizing the expected value of information gained from pre-snap defensive alignments.

primitives.name: Provenance Tagging Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: §0 — How to read this dossier Provenance tags (used everywhere): - [2P] — second-party salary (The Huddle "DFS Fantasy Domination: Week 2," published 2026-09-19; or DK Network Week 2 rankings/salaries, dated 2026-09-15).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: [2P]: Dimensionless provenance flag indicating secondary data source; Salary: USD (United States Dollars)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes secondary sources maintain a bounded error margin relative to primary lobby data before lock time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the secondary source introduces systemic bias or fails to update pre-lock changes, rendering the proxy invalid.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSI's data integrity layer, establishing the foundational prior variance for all subsequent financial constraints in the optimization engine.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of [2P] tags vs lobby-verified tags; deviation between [2P] and actual lock salaries.

primitives.name: Endpoint Blockage Flag
primitives.verbatim_quote: The DK endpoint was Akamai-blocked on 2026-09-19, so no salary in this dossier is lobby-verified.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Akamai-blocked: Boolean network status; Lobby-verified: Binary truth value for data authenticity
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that an unreachable primary API endpoint forces a complete reliance on stale or secondary priors without ground truth.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if the block persists past lineup lock, making exact optimal budget allocation mathematically impossible.

layer2.mapping: Derives a forced uncertainty kernel in GSI, expanding the confidence bounds of all salary inputs by a predefined network-failure penalty factor.
layer2.telemetry: API latency logs; percentage of roster slots populated with unverified cost basis.

primitives.name: Market Strength Tier Gap
primitives.verbatim_quote: Public OWS/DKN ownership figures cover the 13game Sunday main slate, not Garrett's 15-game contest.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Delta_{tier}: Dimensionless rating differential; \mathcal{R}: Objective team rating (0-100 scale)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes objective ratings accurately reflect underlying win probability and dictate game script dynamics like blowout risks.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when highly motivated underdogs defy market pricing, or when early scoring drastically alters the predicted game script.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's game-script predictor, where large tier gaps (>20 points) mathematically collapse the usage distribution of the underdog's passing offense.
layer2.telemetry: Actual point differentials vs predicted tier gaps; underdog passing volume in games with >20 point tier gaps.

primitives.name: Environmental Passing Penalty
primitives.verbatim_quote: † = derived flag (usage profile implies the band; directional, not verified).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: E[FP_{pass}]: Expected fantasy points from passing; W: Wind speed (mph); \alpha: Empirical decay constant
primitives.assumptions: Assumes wind speeds exceeding a specific threshold (e.g., >13 mph) exponentially suppress deep passing success rates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in domed stadiums or if a team employs an exclusively short-passing/checkdown scheme regardless of weather.

layer2.mapping: Feeds directly into GSE's play-calling probability matrix, reducing the transition weight toward deep route concepts and elevating rushing volume priors.
layer2.telemetry: Passing yards per attempt in games with >15 mph sustained winds; shift in rushing share during adverse weather.

primitives.name: Scheme-Defense Alignment Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Christian McCaffrey GOOD: 90% zone-scheme vs MIA's 65.2 zone yards allowed — the strongest true-lead-back preferred-scheme edge on the slate (66% XFP share).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P(S_i | RB): Conditional probability of run scheme (dimensionless); Y_allowed(D_i): Defensive yards allowed in scheme i (yards); \mu_{league}(D_i): League mean yards allowed (yards).
primitives.assumptions: Defensive grading scales linearly with expected yardage loss; historical scheme tendencies remain invariant during the current game state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when defensive scheme variance approaches zero (pure shell defense), rendering the conditional probability undefined or trivial.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE's situational advantage kernel, translating static scheme percentages into dynamic EPA gains per play.
layer2.telemetry: Observed Yards After Contact (YAC) and success rate on zone runs.

primitives.name: Tempo-Driven State Evolution
primitives.verbatim_quote: Tempo: NYJ 5.2 sec/play (2nd-fastest); NYJ six-up rate 3.5% (32nd, lowest).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Psi: Game state vector (dimensionless); \tau: Average time between plays (seconds); \mathbf{A}: Transition matrix dependent on tempo.
primitives.assumptions: Game state evolution is piecewise deterministic between snap events; tempo acts as a scaling factor on the transition matrix eigenvalues.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down during extreme clock-management phases (e.g., two-minute drill) where \tau becomes highly stochastic and non-stationary.

layer2.mapping: Derives the effective sample size of defensive substitutions, feeding directly into GSI's Bayesian updating of defensive fatigue priors.
layer2.telemetry: Actual seconds per play and substitution frequency logs.

primitives.name: Blitz Rate Exploitation Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: identity question (Gannon, ex-Eagles); 3.4% explosive (3rd), 80.2 zone rating (4th), -5.00 INT luck — LEAN-GOOD for NYJ (a 48% blitz rate is exploitable by hot reads if the rate is real).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: V_hot: Expected value of hot read (fantasy points); T_TT: Time to throw (seconds); \Omega_blitz: Subset of defensive looks constituting a blitz.
primitives.assumptions: Quarterback cognitive processing time is constant; blitz identification probability is perfectly correlated with pre-snap diagnostic speed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when defensive disguise effectiveness neutralizes pre-snap identification, causing the indicator function \mathbb{I} to collapse randomly.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the GSE pressure-survival operator, quantifying the exact EPA uplift generated by high-leverage pass-rush failures.
layer2.telemetry: Time to throw (TTT) on blitzes and completion percentage over expected (CPOE).

primitives.name: Mechanical Value Gradient
primitives.verbatim_quote: Caleb Douglas ($3,700): 79.7 mean pool percentile — the #1 mechanical value.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \nabla \mathcal{V}: Value gradient (points per dollar); XFP: Expected fantasy points; Salary: Player cost (dollars); \sigma^2_{pool}: Pool ownership variance.
primitives.assumptions: Market salary is an unbiased estimator of consensus expected output; utility functions are strictly concave regarding ownership percentage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Gradient vanishes at market equilibrium where price perfectly reflects talent-adjusted expected output across all solvers.

layer2.mapping: Feeds the GSI optimization layer, identifying convex regions in the portfolio space where marginal ROI exceeds league average.
layer2.telemetry: Actual ownership percentage and resulting tournament finish rates.

primitives.name: Injury-Induced Target Consolidation

primitives.assumptions: Target distribution is inversely proportional to coverage unit strength; injury status is deterministic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: T_c ∝ 1/P_{cov} when I_{inj} = 1

primitives.name: Blitz Rate Influence on Receiver Efficiency

reasoning_traces.think:
The mathematical foundation of the Week 2 DFS dossier rests on constructing a robust optimization landscape despite severe information asymmetry. The primary constraint is the salary cap, but the coefficients representing player costs are inherently noisy due to the Akamai blockage of the primary DraftKings endpoint. This forces the system to rely entirely on second-party ([2P]) priors. In a Bayesian framework, the [2P] tag represents a prior distribution $P(Salary | Source)$ with an elevated variance term compared to lobby-verified data. The dossier explicitly quantifies this epistemic uncertainty, preventing the solver from treating these numbers as hard constants.

Simultaneously, the projection engine must account for dynamic state transitions driven by external variables. The 'blowout-risk tier gaps' derived from @benbbaldwin's objective ratings function as a macro-level filter on the game script. A gap such as BAL (65.2) vs NO (41.0) mathematically implies a truncated timeline for the underdog's offensive possessions, effectively zeroing out the expected value of certain low-floor assets late in the game. This is modeled via a time-decay function applied to possession-based projections.

Furthermore, micro-level perturbations—specifically weather and injuries—act as localized operators on the adjacency matrix of the offensive scheme. The Chicago game's wind and rain introduce a non-linear penalty to deep passing routes, shifting the probability mass toward running backs and check-down receivers. Similarly, Okonkwo's absence creates a vacuum in Washington's tight end group, mathematically redistributing his historical target share (14% TPRR) to adjacent nodes like Jake Ferguson or local replacements. The sovereign primitive here is the synthesis of these disparate signals—network failures, macro-tier gaps, and micro-environmental shifts—into a unified, continuously updated expected value surface that dictates optimal roster construction.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This analytical framework descends from early 2010s poker equity calculators adapted for daily fantasy sports. Initially, DFS relied on static historical averages. The introduction of real-time injury protocols (like McCarthy's concussion status) and live weather APIs necessitated a shift toward dynamic, conditional probability models. The explicit tagging of data provenance ([2P], [FLAG]) evolved as a direct response to the 2023-2024 era of increasing sportsbook API restrictions and Akamai blocking, forcing analysts to mathematically quantify the degradation of their input data quality.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The dossier implicitly models the opposing agents—the public pool and the DFS site algorithms. By noting that public ownership figures only cover the 13-game main slate, the analyst anticipates a collinearity trap: the public will heavily concentrate on the 13 standard games, leaving the two additional games in Garrett's 15-game contest as a low-ownership, high-upside frontier. Furthermore, recognizing that Dak Prescott faced significant pressure (-0.52 EPA/db) allows the analyst to predict how opposing defenses will continue to exploit this weakness, adjusting the expected defensive load on CeeDee Lamb accordingly.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition exists between the environmental layer and the schematic layer. If the wind in Chicago exceeds 30 mph, the 'checkdown premium' assumption might break down entirely, potentially leading to a run-heavy, clock-killing script that negates even the rushing volume upside. Additionally, if Carson Wentz's performance deviates significantly from his baseline, the entire Minnesota offensive tree collapses, rendering Jefferson's elite route-running metrics irrelevant. The system must continuously monitor these cross-layer dependencies to prevent cascading errors in the final lineup optimization.
